chunks: Muhammad ibn Isa reported it, from Yaseen al-Darir, from Hariz, from Al-Fudayl, who said:

I performed Hajj with my family one year, and the sacrificial animals were expensive. So I went and bought two sheep for a high price. So, when I examined their cuticles, I regretted it with an intense regret due to what I saw with them from the thinness. So I went over to him and informed him of that. So he said: ‘If there was something from the fat upon their kidneys, they would both suffice’.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a thin sacrificial animal to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of the Udhiyah (sacrificial animal) is not strictly contingent upon overall robustness or high cost, but rather on the presence of specific physical markers of health, such as fat on the kidneys (al-kawya). It reflects the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing for the acceptance of leaner animals if they meet the essential criteria for sacrifice, thereby alleviating the burden on pilgrims during years of scarcity or high prices.
